where-the-river-begins.rationale: "Gritty" naturalist migration drama with non-professional Indigenous cast, displacement and paramilitary violence, but "more poetic and more poignant" than urgent thriller.

the-daughters-of-abraham.rationale: Naturalistic French-language debut about estranged Muslim and Jewish friends whose reunion is broken by "an unexpected tragedy" — an "incisive study of faith and gender" called "propulsive" but essentially intimate drama.

nobodys-violence.rationale: Wavelengths Côté euthanasia dystopia that "shape-shifts from sci-fi parable to conspiracy thriller to Buñuelian comedy" with "restless, relentless vitality" across 148 French-language minutes.

re-pair.rationale: Conversation-driven doc of "19 different pairings" of Black and Jewish figures, "respect, candor, and humour," tackling antisemitism and Israel/Palestine at 131 talky minutes.

blindspot-berlin.rationale: "A compelling procedural thriller" reconstructing the 2016 Breitscheidplatz attack, "unflinching" and heavy with surveillance and radicalization, in German/Arabic/Turkish.

in-waves.rationale: Animated graphic-novel adaptation about cancer and loss, "gentle coming-of-age" with water rendered as sacred element — slow, heavy, formally distinctive via 2D/3D animation, in English.

smudge-the-blades.rationale: A "dramedy" underdog hockey movie in the Bad News Bears mould, "grittier and more dramatic" with "high-energy hockey play" and laughs, set on a Northern Alberta reserve.

love-is-the-monster.rationale: "Bold tropical dystopian" kidnapping thriller "mixing elements of genre storytelling," tense and "deeply unsettling" vision of inequality, in Spanish with Paulina García.

pretenders.rationale: Conventional archival-and-interview music doc on Chrissie Hynde, "tough, stylish" with "thrilling performance footage" and a tragedy at its centre.

at-night.rationale: Wavelengths debut feature of "poetic, collaborative autofiction" that "boldly transcends traditional narrative," shifting between narrative, documentary, and dream on 16mm, melancholic and multilingual.

darlene-love-i-know-where-ive-been.rationale: Conventional "high-spirited, warm-hearted" talking-head music doc with performance sequences, buoyed by hits but running a long 145 minutes.

in-conversation-with-andrew-scott.rationale: A live on-stage career conversation with Andrew Scott, exploring "the remarkable range of Scott's career" — nonfiction talk event, no narrative form.

the-bovine-with-the-curved-horns.rationale: Magical-realist child's-eye view of paramilitary terror in the Ciénaga Grande, with non-professional cast, myth and "cadence of rhythms of daily life," unfolding "poetically" in nuanced black-and-white.

a-good-little-soldier.rationale: French social realism on "the alienating, dehumanizing consequences of capitalist structures," conventional in form with "searing performances" from Rohrwacher and Lindon.

the-secret-lives-of-baba-segis-wives.rationale: "Sharp, funny, and often devastating" Nollywood family drama that shifts between wives' perspectives, using humour to expose "deep wounds caused by infertility, sexual exploitation" across 149 minutes.

in-the-heart-of-the-south.rationale: "Crackling" psychological thriller of doubling and infiltration, "thrilling, stylish, funny" with sharp satire of the Toronto art world's treatment of Indigenous artists.

oxygen-masks-will-not-drop-automatically.rationale: 1980s Brazilian AIDS drama where "joy and dread were intertwined" — neon club vibrancy against stigma and death, conventional narrative in Portuguese at 140 min.

minotaur.rationale: Zvyagintsev's Cannes Grand Prix winner, 171 minutes of glacial Krichman-shot moral rot about conscription quotas — "a devastating work" with a thriller undertow of blood on his hands.

strong-son-2.rationale: Character-driven debut about a bodybuilder "trapped in a quagmire of anxiety and insecurity" caregiving for his father, with "teary public breakdowns" and Sikh family dynamics, largely English with some Punjabi.

silenced-nights.rationale: A "bleak drama" of Manila drug-war killings shot cinéma vérité in the Happyland slum, driven by an investigation that keeps hitting "brick walls."

rehearsals-for-a-revolution.rationale: Essayistic first-person documentary "mining memory" through home movies and news footage across five chapters of Iranian political trauma, Cannes L'Œil d'Or winner.

eklipse.rationale: "Poetic realism" coming-of-age in rural 1999 Austria, German-language, with VHS footage blending reality and fiction and a father's hidden illness driving quiet heaviness.

furies.rationale: A 164-minute Arabic-language Beirut heist thriller with "fast-paced editing" and a "thrilling race against the clock," rooted in the bleak reality of Lebanon's banking collapse.

river.rationale: "Audacious nerve-shredder" slasher debut with a featureless Shape-like killer, austere suspense and "pastoral surrealism" seeping into a claustrophobic open-water siege.

all-of-a-sudden.rationale: 226-minute Hamaguchi "cinema of words" built on extended dialogue about illness and caregiving, shot in a working care facility with real patients in French and Japanese.

arrested-memory.rationale: SABU's "genre farce" of "multi-pronged chases," dance numbers and bumbling cops and Yakuza — a kinetic Mandarin/Japanese comic action romp with a melancholy undertow of guilt and memory loss.

kick-on.rationale: A "bloody ripper of a siege thriller" of "ultraviolence" and body-horror gags recalling Green Room, tension "gleefully stretched" over a single Melbourne night.

le-faux-soir.rationale: A "fleet-footed and thoroughly entertaining" WWII resistance thriller with "all the pace and panache of a classic heist movie," in French at 163 min, from Bullhead director Roskam.

angh.rationale: "Haunting and intimate" 16mm debut in Konyak language, observational and unsentimental about missionary conversion, slow and spatially sound-driven at 133 min.

seventeen.rationale: Ticking-clock naturalist drama of three queer Indigenous sex workers over 17 hours in "gritty downtown Vancouver," heavy and conventional in form, mostly English with some Cree.

spring-in-a-small-town.rationale: "Poetic, romantic 1948 masterpiece" of repressed desire told in "long takes, careful framing, and suggestive lighting," a canonical Chinese classic in 4K restoration.

intermission.rationale: A 255-minute "neither documentary nor conventional film-on-film essay" montage-memoir of Yonfan's 15 films, "conceived almost like a musical compilation" with virtuoso circular editing.

trash-mountain.rationale: "Funny, wise" homecoming comedy that "overflows with irreverence and tenderness" — conventional indie dramedy with real grief underneath.

a-long-winter.rationale: Haigh's "patient, intimate filmmaking" and Tóibín's "measured storytelling" where "every silence, glance, and gesture carries extraordinary weight" over a 147-min family grief drama.

our-loves.rationale: A 147-minute Hebrew/Arabic "dramatic network narrative" of interwoven personal griefs that turns to catastrophe and communal survival, "moving and profound" rather than kinetic.

my-wife-cries.rationale: Schanelec's "austere and solemn" 35mm elegy of "emotional distance and anguish," with "painterly still life compositions" and eccentric intrusions, is deep-contemplative art cinema in German.

tehran-under-the-skin.rationale: Observational Persian-language doc embedded with Tehran cosmetic surgeons, bringing "curiosity, humour, and empathy," with political violence lurking in the background and a "sparing and stylish" approach to the operating room.

how-we-stand.rationale: A "riveting drama of sisters" shaped by Indigenous relocation policy, heavy with trauma and sexual violence but lifted by magic realism and "a dose of humour" sending up Hollywood westerns.

diary-of-a-mad-old-man.rationale: A "delicate" chamber drama of "beguiling signals and unruly desire" between a paralyzed widower and his caregiver daughter-in-law, in Japanese/Mandarin at 145 min.

the-unknown.rationale: "Moody, existential body-swap puzzler, drenched in atmospheric dread," 170 min Cannes Competition highlight, "labyrinthine and unsettling" with Lynch/De Palma comparisons and a "sense of despair."

stuffed.rationale: A "twisted musical" dark comedy of taxidermy and longing, "gleefully" macabre and heightened, with Jodie Comer, running a long 147 min at a premium premiere.

bitter-christmas.rationale: Almodóvar's "house of mirrors" of stories within stories, with "noirish hues and telenovale twists" and sumptuous colour, exploring grief, love, and artistic licence.

back-in-black.rationale: A "deliciously macabre black comedy" and "sabre-toothed satire" with Walken's foul-mouthed mortician and small-town murder "accidents" — conventional narrative, huge comic register, mild genre darkness.

cheyenne.rationale: Conventional sports doc following four bronc riders with "adrenaline-pumping rodeo action" plus quieter camaraderie, past trauma, and gender double standards.

still-night-burning-house.rationale: A "personal documentary" on an uncle's suicide, "deeply affecting and visually stunning," quiet family grief work moving between Toronto and Vietnam.

we-are-all-strangers.rationale: Anthony Chen's 187-minute closing chapter of his Growing Up trilogy: a slow, humanist family drama of "emotional journey and growing pains" and class divides, largely in Mandarin.

half.rationale: A vampire "curry western" of "guts and gore" with The Raid 2's action choreographer, "maul, maim, and murder" revenge across Rajasthan in multiple Indian languages.

once-upon-a-time-in-harlem.rationale: A "rapturous living archive" of Harlem Renaissance luminaries shot on multiple 16mm cameras at a 1972 party, structureless and conversational with "humour, fervour... and not a bit of melancholy."

onwards-and-sideways.rationale: Conventional British illness dramedy with "heartache, laughter, and hard-won connection" — sober look at degenerative disease leavened by irreverent humour, at a comfortable Gala 140 minutes.

voices.rationale: Single-location "noir-ish" 1967 Detroit musical about a desperate con, with "infectious musical reveries" lifting the register from its claustrophobic, corrupting-fame darkness.

soumsoum-the-night-of-the-stars.rationale: Haroun's Ennedi-set tale of an ostracized visionary girl takes "a realistic approach to the fantasy genre," contemplative and mythic, in Arabic and French, with heavy themes of exclusion and the dead.

the-assassins.rationale: A 161-minute "large-canvas procedural" and "suspenseful tale" about political conspiracy, conventionally told with set pieces and multi-threaded storytelling, in Korean and Japanese.

short-cuts-2026-programme-03.rationale: Note is boilerplate mission statement with no film detail; placements are generic Short Cuts averages — mixed forms, some subtitled work, anthology of varied registers.

in-conversation-with-lee-min-ho.rationale: A live onstage career conversation with "global Hallyu icon Lee Min-ho" — not a film at all, closest to nonfiction talk with Korean-language cultural context.

children-untold.rationale: A 180-minute neorealist "portrait of childhood stolen by war" in postwar Tokyo, unsentimental about "abandonment, abused childhoods," from an established Japanese auteur with Koji Yakusho.

brace-your-heart.rationale: An "intimate, layered" Sámi-language love story shaped by "the rhythms of reindeer herding," built from "the smallest of gestures" and landscapes, with mistreatment and endurance at its heart.

paradise-lost.rationale: A "gripping psychological thriller" from Train to Busan's Yeon Sang-ho, "at times frightening exploration of human darkness and trauma" about maternal grief, in Korean.

conversation-with-the-sea.rationale: A "social commentary and personal quest" of grief and bureaucratic injustice in Jerusalem, 142 min, Arabic/Hebrew, with "meticulous direction" and a "remorse-ridden antihero."

ben-imana.rationale: Rwandan gacaca-court drama on genocide trauma and forced motherhood, "powerful intergenerational narrative" in Kinyarwanda, Caméra d'Or winner at 131 min.

inherit.rationale: Thai occult horror from the director of Pee Mak, "scares remain sleek and strong" but with "heavier themes of corruption, exploitation" woven into family drama across 158 minutes.

coward.rationale: Dhont's 155-min WWI trench love story, Cannes Best Actor winner, trading spectacle for "intimacy, specificity, and humanity" amid "the First World War's many horrors."

bad-lieutenant-tokyo.rationale: Miike's "rollercoaster ride through the darkest crevasses of the Tokyo underworld" — an "intricately plotted crime odyssey" of "shameless sensationalism," bilingual English/Japanese.

memories-of-a-forest.rationale: Quiet German-language rural family drama about inheritance and duty, a "stunning debut" of landscape and laconic feeling rather than incident.

turtle-island-rap.rationale: Cinéma vérité music doc following three Indigenous rappers "from the hustle to the stage," with "warmth and humour, even when things are tough."

all-that-she-wants.rationale: "Effervescent, tender-hearted, refreshingly modern" rom-com that's "sexy, hilarious" — conventional crowd-pleasing comedy with light emotional stakes.

up-against-it.rationale: "Wickedly clever comedy" and "inventive spin on the screwball comedy" built around a child's leukemia, star-driven Gala at 152 minutes.

a-common-story.rationale: Quiet Italian empty-nest drama that "lingers in each gesture and every moment of silence," a 137-minute intimate debut with Alba Rohrwacher.

sunburn.rationale: A "loose, funny" hang-out coming-of-age film in the spirit of Dazed and Confused, sweaty and vibrant but plotless and low-stakes.

low-lies-the-land.rationale: Observational Italian vineyard doc with "exquisite compositions" and a "slow-burn suspense" over land sales, akin to The Truffle Hunters.

hope.rationale: "Marathon of breathless set pieces" with monster-movie spectacle, "harrowing and hilarious" comedy, and an epic-tragedy turn across 167 Korean-language minutes from Na Hong-jin.

josephine.rationale: A "devastating portrait" of a traumatized child at 149 minutes, using "formal rigour and grounded direction" and subjective camerawork to render paranoia rather than genre thrills.

thirteen-in-gaza.rationale: Intimate Gaza-shot coming-of-age drama in a displacement camp "devoid of safety, privacy, and care," observational and heavy rather than sensationalistic.

the-city-of-the-living.rationale: An "anti-true crime film" that "delicately explores" the social dynamics behind a young man's murder — sombre, character-led Italian drama rather than thriller, though the violence keeps some genre charge.

we-are-born-good.rationale: An "escalating feud" comedy-drama with "narrative momentum" and humour, set among debt-crushed Hong Kongers "worn down by grief, anger, and exhaustion."

run-terry-run.rationale: Archival-driven "intimate and inspiring portrait" of Terry Fox's Marathon of Hope — conventional documentary, emotionally heavy given his death, 138 min gala.

it-will-happen-tonight.rationale: "Exuberant" multi-decade romantic ensemble from Italian auteur Moretti, "charming" and warm-hearted with wry comic register, largely Italian-language conventional narrative.

four-seasons-in-java.rationale: Andini's "most ambitious yet" 167-minute female-centred drama on sexual violence, blending fantasy and "breathtaking visuals" with "deep metaphors," demanding and bleak.

black-sunflowers.rationale: A "mosaic" doc of Ukrainian twentysomethings from dance clubs to frontline barracks, "youthful spirit" and drifting energy balanced against tragedy and duty, by a music-video visualist.

in-alaska.rationale: A "tense and darkly humorous" Arctic manhunt drama about a depressed Inuk teen labelled an eco-terrorist, partly in Inuktitut, with hostile nature and mental-health weight.

ink.rationale: "Fast-paced and gripping" Boyle adaptation of a stage play about The Sun's tabloid rise, stylish and kinetic with dark satirical bite.

crystal-lake.rationale: A24 Friday the 13th origin series: "a moving portrait of a mother consumed with grief" plus "a very high body count" and "a bloody good time."

what-lies-between-us.rationale: A "provocative and gripping" Danish moral drama about mothers and a sexual assault accusation, "expertly paced" and conventionally told, with heavy themes and strong performances.

salvation.rationale: Assured Scottish debut about a delusional would-be life coach — social-realist character study we "cringe at" with "unnerving depth," lightly comic but sincere and desperate.

flies.rationale: Eimbcke's black-and-white, "unhurried," "understated mise en scène" portrait of a lonely woman finding chosen family, with "moments of humour, grace, and quiet revelation in the everyday."

gentle-monster.rationale: Kreutzer's "measured handling of this freighted material" makes a chilling, bleak domestic drama about sex crimes in the family, in German with a major premiere and 144-minute runtime.

long-long-night.rationale: "Radiant animation" fable of a rhino and penguin, "alternating between mirth and profound loss" with poachers and tragedy, Korean-language Centrepiece debut.

i-am-mario.rationale: Naturalistic Mexican debut about a pregnant trans man "completely cornered by life," dignified and slow-burning social drama with transphobic language and explicit sex.

the-beloved.rationale: A 165-minute Sorogoyen drama of "cruelty, manipulation, and the reopening of old wounds" between estranged father and daughter on a film shoot — "darker" and "more brutal" than Sentimental Value.

bunker.rationale: Talky Zeller marriage drama of "affluence, paranoia, and ambition" at 156 min, mostly English with Cruz/Bardem star power and a paranoid-thriller edge.

anchors-aweigh.rationale: An "essayistic" mock-doc parody of Sherman's March with "deadpan punchlines" in a Nathan Fielder register — surreal vignettes, laugh-out-loud alt-comedy rather than Midnight genre.

ken-russells-the-devils.rationale: "Feverish," transgressive Russell provocation staging "mass hysteria, torture, and exorcism as history, horror, and political allegory" in baroque excess with body horror.

short-cuts-2026-programme-04.rationale: Note is boilerplate mission statement with no content; placements are generic Short Cuts averages — mixed-form shorts anthology at 130 min.

the-black-box-is-orange.rationale: A "multimodal, autobiographical essay film" in 10 stylistically distinct chapters with hand-processed 16mm and contrapuntal sound, reckoning with the Nakba, occupation, and complicit memory.

club-kid.rationale: Firstman's "spirited debut" club-scene comedy-drama that "bops to familiar beats" toward "emotional catharsis" as a "consummate crowd pleaser," with Cannes buzz and a 152-min runtime.

the-lost-children-of-tuam.rationale: A "deeply humane drama" of "painstaking archival work" and "patient persistence" about 796 dead infants — restrained, conventional, and heavy, with English-language Irish setting.

the-violinist.rationale: Sweeping animated wartime romance spanning eight decades, "an emotional ride, traversing loss, remembrance, resilience," at 144 min with Annecy's Cristal top prize.

bedford-park.rationale: "Powerful and raw" 151-minute debut drama of generational trauma and cultural displacement, slow-building relationship study in English and Korean.

its-my-time.rationale: Crowd-pleasing Mandarin/Cantonese Gala comedy with Michelle Yeoh, "warmth and deep emotion" plus regrets, conventional inspirational-competition narrative at 137 min.

pelechian-project.rationale: Wordless "visually and musically maximalist" montage documentaries with "passages of pure exhilaration," each "a harrowing ode to humanity" — formally radical nonfiction, newly restored.

ha-chan-shake-your-booty.rationale: A "stylized melange of melodrama and fantasia" about grief in Tokyo — quirky, fleet-footed and playful with fantasy interludes (a colossal crow, Dirty Dancing), largely Japanese/Spanish-language at 151 min.

carrie.rationale: Flanagan's King adaptation is a straight-ahead horror of "high school as humiliation ritual," building to prom carnage — heightened genre, heavy, conventionally told.

american-hostage.rationale: Fact-based hostage stand-off thriller about radio ethics, "murky boundaries between participant and observer," conventional Primetime series with tense but talk-driven procedural energy.

the-difficult-bride.rationale: Bengali-language Centrepiece body-horror-inflected drama "awash in striking images" of catfish, snakes, and things moving under skin, dwelling on a bride's asphyxiating pressures rather than plot momentum.

hombre-al-agua.rationale: A "psychologically astute comedy of manners" about class and social advancement, Spanish/Portuguese ensemble piece at 146 min, wry and ambiance-driven rather than propulsive.

god-bless-you-mr-kopu.rationale: "Sharp social satire" with "swagger of late-1970s hustler and action cinema" that builds into a "propulsive thriller," a dark comedy in mostly English with Tongan cultural specificity.

edward-said-between-worlds.rationale: Archival-driven portrait "in Said's own words" braiding hundreds of hours of interviews, weighty on Palestine and the Nakba, mostly English with some Arabic, 137 min.

the-hummingbird-paints-fragrant-songs.rationale: A "poetic and experiential" Spanish/Shipibo-language artist portrait that leaves "viewers to draw their own interpretations," moving between Amazon patrols and art-world champagne.

fjord.rationale: Palme d'Or-winning Mungiu: a 176-minute "intricate, gripping courtroom drama driven by a profound moral dilemma," mostly Romanian/Norwegian dialogue and severe in register.

the-perverts-guide-to-utopias.rationale: "Free-flowing essay" film staging Žižek inside recreated movie tableaus — "a heady intellectual ride, infused with mischief and glee" at 163 minutes.

the-smell-of-apples.rationale: "Relentless" apartheid-era coming-of-horror told from the beneficiary's view, Afrikaans-language, "a brilliant exploration of human baseness" — heavy, slow-burn, conventionally narrated.

man-in-motion-the-rick-hansen-story.rationale: Conventional archival-and-interview Gala documentary "celebration" of Rick Hansen's Man in Motion tour, inspirational rather than bleak or formally adventurous.

elephants-in-the-fog.rationale: "Fierce but tender debut" with non-actors, "exquisitely rendered images of the verdant setting" and a slow tension between tradition and modernity in a Nepali third-gender community.

wavelengths-anoushahpour-aljafari.rationale: Two "unhurried" Wavelengths essay-documentaries on memory and imagination, one Kurdish-village embroidery portrait, one "understated" observational study of Masao Adachi's passport attempt.

kissed.rationale: "Ethereal atmosphere" akin to Crash and Exotica, a dreamy, trance-like drama of necrophilia that balances "reality and fantasy" rather than playing as horror.

everybody-wants-to-fck-me.rationale: "Darkly comedic debut" satire of "nice guys" with "genuinely intense moments" and an absurdist escalation into stalking and "vigorous pursuit," no easy redemptions.

the-life-and-deaths-of-wilson-shedd.rationale: "Psychologically rich prison story about crime, punishment, and love" in Oklahoma, 151 min of abusive marriage and incarceration — heavy, conventional character drama with star performances.

short-cuts-2026-programme-02.rationale: Note is only TIFF's boilerplate mission statement, so placement rests entirely on the Short Cuts prior: a mixed 131-min shorts block of varied tone and language.

drifter.rationale: An "existential action film" that's "by turns melancholy and exhilarating" — real drifting spectacle wrapped in a soulful, grief-laden character study stretched across 177 minutes.

london.rationale: An "experimental road movie" of static car conversations shot with vintage rear-projection, 150 min of "existential colloquy" in German inspired by James Benning.

possible-love.rationale: Lee Chang-dong's 194-minute return, a "tale of deep yearning, envy, and grief" whose "small revelations" accumulate quietly around class and power.

the-julia-set.rationale: Conventional character-driven drama about a math prodigy and competition pressure, "insightful debut" with strong cast, 142 min of talky institutional tension rather than kinetic incident.

making-waves-with-hudson-williams.rationale: Not a film but an "intimate conversation" with actor Hudson Williams for TIFF Next Wave, a talk-format event with no cinematic form of its own.

spirit-guardians-the-last-secret-of-the-.rationale: A 181-minute Vietnamese historical epic "reminiscent of Kurosawa," "bracingly visceral" with "breathtaking martial arts choreography" and sumptuous pageantry.

short-cuts-2026-strange-cuts.rationale: No substantive note; inferred from a Short Cuts shorts programme titled "Strange Cuts," suggesting genre-tinged, formally offbeat work of varied origin.

the-stunt-driver.rationale: "Raucous yet heartfelt" biopic comedy matching the "anarchic energy" of Goon, with car stunts and poignancy beneath the bravado.

the-dreamed-adventure.rationale: A 194-minute Bulgarian-language "masterful slow-burn" of smuggling and memory from Grisebach, Cannes Jury Prize winner, with crime plot points as "blips in something bigger and more nebulous."

bucking-fastard.rationale: Herzog's first narrative feature in years, a strange tale of twins who "speak in unison" and share a lover — eccentric, quasi-mythic register with courtroom melodrama, English-language and star-driven.

the-debut.rationale: "Rich, dark comedy from the self-seriousness of community theatre" — a conventional, performance-driven dramedy, "hilarious and smart from beginning to end."

the-spiral.rationale: A "riveting psychological chiller" in four chapters, "enveloped in a pervasive pall of unblinking dread" — Faustian supernatural horror, Italian-language, 145 min of slow screw-turning.

dorothy.rationale: A 180-minute Tamil "wild ride" that "leaps across genres" combining noir thriller, gangster, romance and Bruce Lee action with Hawksian physical comedy, set amid "everyday violence" and patriarchal oppression.

mr-nelson-did-you-kill-people.rationale: Tsukamoto war film with "relentless narrative momentum" and "visceral visual language," "fierce, harrowing" trauma portrait with explicit violence and strobing, mostly English at 146 min.

like-magic.rationale: Personal essay-doc weaving "a vast trove of archival footage with testimonies" about cartel-era Cali violence, reflective and heavy rather than propulsive.

ten-dark-women.rationale: Ichikawa's "stylish, satirical" noir-melodrama inversion with "modernist jazz," "formal precision," and "sardonic humour," restored in 4K — a classic revival with genre codes played for cynical comedy.

the-only-living-pickpocket-in-new-york.rationale: "Low-key crime drama" with a "meditation on changing times" in the character-driven 1970s New Hollywood mode, carried by Turturro's charm.

vintage-violence.rationale: "Chronically online" V-Cinema-style caper with screen-collage form, "madcap hijinks," ultraviolence and Tokyo foot chases — fast, funny, stylized genre.

wavelengths-3-time-and-tide.rationale: Wavelengths shorts programme of 65mm formalism, Baroque illusionism, archival 8mm Roma footage and a Duras/Conrad-inspired essay — avowedly experimental and contemplative.

being-heumann.rationale: Crowd-pleasing 157-min activist biopic from CODA's Siân Heder, "every bit as moving" and conventionally told, with the momentum of an occupation campaign.

wild-horse-nine.rationale: McDonagh black comedy of "eccentric CIA agents" with "signature incisive dialogue," paranoia and dark reckoning across 148 minutes on Easter Island.

tender-loving-care.rationale: Leigh's "astute portrait of ordinary lives" on aging and family — "poignant without ever becoming sentimental" and "unflinchingly real without becoming grim," with plenty of laughter.

after-elena.rationale: A "gentle, non-judgmental" Spanish-language family grief drama that "doesn't wallow in heaviness," finding richness in small gestures with "humour, melancholy," and "absurd situations."

love-of-your-life.rationale: "Sweeping romantic character study" of love and loss, "by turns soulful, heartbreaking, and wise," conventional narrative over years and continents in English at 136 min.

rescue.rationale: Vérité migrant-rescue doc that opens with "a harrowing abduction" and plays so dramatically "you frequently need to remind yourself that it's a documentary," mostly Arabic with cell-phone footage from captivity.

everest-the-other-side.rationale: Chin/Vasarhelyi IMAX adventure doc of "spectacle and emotion," high-stakes Everest ski descent shadowed by death, in the Free Solo register but longer and heavier.

slow-horses.rationale: TV spy thriller episodes with "propulsive energy and dark humour," "quick-witted and always entertaining ride" through espionage.

alpha-gang.rationale: Deadpan Zellner brothers sci-fi comedy where aliens in '50s leather jackets are undone by "moments of intimacy, art, joy, and sadness," with "creative humour" and a starry cast.

in-conversation-with-chris-rock.rationale: A live onstage talk with Chris Rock about his "multi-faceted career" — nonfiction event in a comic register, no narrative form.

in-conversation-with-rachel-morrison.rationale: Live onstage conversation with Oscar-nominated cinematographer-director Rachel Morrison about her "remarkable journey" — nonfiction talk, no dramatic form, craft-focused rather than heavy or genre.

the-face-of-horror.rationale: Anna Biller's "wickedly camp" 150-minute 35mm pastiche of Technicolor shockers — heightened gory genre with "pervasively wry wit" over sincere melodrama, stylized rather than propulsive.

babies.rationale: A star-studded, "relatable, hilarious, and wise" mainstream ensemble comedy about whether to have kids — conventional, big-hearted, low stakes.

glaxo.rationale: Naishtat's multi-timeline Argentinian revenge drama, "suspenseful story unfolds gradually," "deeply atmospheric," with an "intense, uncompromising look" at national violence.

rapinoe.rationale: A sports-star doc handed to Beba's Rebeca Huntt for a "bold and original" treatment — playful, introspective, family-dynamics-decoding rather than conventional hagiography.

congo-boy.rationale: Handheld "immediacy" and rap-driven "singular rhythms" energize a hustling refugee teen's story in Sango/French/Lingala, weighty but "inspiring" with "colossal heart."

clarissa.rationale: Woolf's Mrs. Dalloway transposed to contemporary Nigeria in 164 min of 35mm interiority — "a suspended moment in time" of "introspection, existential crisis," with PTSD and Boko Haram trauma threaded through.

redefined-short-film-showcase.rationale: Five short personal-storytelling works from Canadian and Indigenous filmmakers exploring "culture, belonging, identity, and sovereign(ties)," suggesting essayistic, largely documentary-leaning form.

short-cuts-2026-programme-06.rationale: Note is boilerplate mission statement with no film detail; placed at neutral defaults for a mixed Short Cuts anthology programme, which tends toward mild formal play and varied language.

all-about-corinne.rationale: A "delectable comedy" of French film-industry meta-hijinks with Huppert as a career extra, stars playing themselves, "playful, absorbing, and rife with insider wit" at 145 minutes.

life-of-jorge-luis-borges.rationale: A 370-minute Wavelengths essay-film by La Flor's Llinás that "blurs the line between the real and the invented," digressive, erudite, playful, and enormously demanding.

bleeding-hearts.rationale: Black-and-white vintage-lens music doc "candid portrait" of a country trio's romance and career strain — observational, emotionally messy but not bleak.

ah-girl.rationale: Autobiographical 1990s Singapore childhood drama with "soft cinematography" and "delicate, hazy" dreamy sequences, mundane detail and "bittersweet déjà vu" over painful family rupture.

the-man-i-love.rationale: Naturalistic AIDS-era portrait that "lingers on impromptu performances, conversations around the dinner table, and long, grounded theatre rehearsal scenes," warm but heavy with the disease's spectre.

obsession.rationale: Monkey's-Paw horror-comedy debut with "wickedly wry tone and an anxious tension" compared to Barbarian, at a hefty 138 min.

djinn-wedding.rationale: An "atmospheric family drama" over three life stages, 162 min, with a long-take wedding centrepiece and "just the right amount of mystery," heavy with patriarchy and buried memory.

everytime.rationale: Grief drama in a "hallucinatory state," shot by Aftersun's DP, from the Un Certain Regard–winning Wollner; 149 slow minutes that "linger well beyond its runtime."

everything-else-is-noise.rationale: A "sly, self-reflexive comedy of manners and mishaps" in Wavelengths, chamber-piece structure with "inspiring economy of form" and Lubitschian light touch, in Spanish at 101 minutes.

tangles.rationale: Hand-drawn 2D animated Alzheimer's memoir, "deeply moving" with heavy material balanced by comic voice cast levity.

wild-wild-east.rationale: "A suspenseful western meets wartime noir" set in 1943 occupied Poland, a web of betrayal and greed among traumatized villagers and Nazi authorities, in Polish/German/Ukrainian at 135 min.

ladies-and-gentlemen-brian-mulroney.rationale: An archival "culture jam" fever dream — "as if Adam Curtis overdosed on a psychic stream of Heritage Minutes" — satirical, collage-based, mostly English with some French.

musk.rationale: Gibney's "most ambitious and epic documentary" at 260 minutes with an "innovative graphic treatment" — a demanding English-language investigative marathon.

alice.rationale: A "sweeping series" period biopic of Alice Guy-Blaché in La Belle Époque Paris, conventional prestige narrative in French with Bérénice Bejo.

the-fortunate-isles.rationale: A "restrained epic of colonial regret" with "tactile camera and uniquely portentous style" — slow, poetic, formally elevated period drama of enslavement and drought, in Spanish/Arabic.

julian.rationale: Cartoon Saloon family animation, "charmingly expressive" with "humour, tenderness," gentle and warm rather than heavy, mostly English with some Spanish.

the-ultra-runner.rationale: "Riveting footage" of an Arctic ultramarathon plus "highly skilful and stylish use of re-enactments" of a Romanian childhood and prison term make this a propulsive, partly subtitled endurance doc.

the-betrayers.rationale: "Gripping and elegant" literary adaptation of moral/political drama in Yalta, largely English but steeped in Soviet-Israeli history, talky and character-driven rather than kinetic.

ashes.rationale: A "mature and nuanced" immigrant drama of displacement and "toughest trials" in Spanish/Catalan, conventionally told with heavy emotional toll.

la-gradiva.rationale: A 175-minute French-Italian ensemble coming-of-age film in Pompeii balancing "visual poetry with an intellectual rigour" and a "documentary-like approach to shooting."

the-housewife.rationale: A 1964-set "psychological historical drama" of Nazi complicity that "shifts from tense thriller to courtroom drama," polished and conventional with heavy themes.

elsinore.rationale: Biographical AIDS-era drama of actor Ian Charleson playing Hamlet, "visceral, profoundly moving" with warmth and wit, powered by Andrew Scott's "career-best performance."

i-play-rocky.rationale: Crowd-pleasing conventional Hollywood biopic that "soars with sweat and spirit" from Green Book's Farrelly, 157 min but propulsive underdog rise.

lautre.rationale: A "darkly comedic thriller about a mind and body in peril," confined to a hospital room but "visceral, sometimes harrowing" with drug-addled unreality and "bristling energy."

rogue-trooper.rationale: Performance-capture 2000 AD military sci-fi with "psychotronic spectacle" and explicit violence, but Jones keeps the comics' "playful, satirical, and surreal" British comic voice via Berry, Clement, Morgan.

look-back.rationale: Kore-eda's tender 35mm live-action of Fujimoto's manga about two girl artists, "unfolding across the four seasons" with "emotional intensity" and grief over life's brevity.

krux.rationale: WWII village atrocity drama of "moral collapse, societal panic" with "haunting visuals," brutal historical violence, German-language debut running 122 minutes.

girl-group.rationale: Crowd-pleasing musical comedy with a "hilarious cast" and "fantastic soundtrack," conventional mentor-redemption arc for a "jaded pop-star burnout."

muyi.rationale: A "charming, imaginative, and visually stunning" French-language animated coming-of-age fable set in China, with whimsical touches like "a vegetarian tiger and a magical guide."

the-age-of-goodbyes.rationale: "Once considered unfilmable," a 172-minute non-linear metafictional adaptation whose timelines "could make it challenging to follow" but is "visually stunning" and rewards rewatching.

gail.rationale: Character-driven "unconventional music doc" following a superfan whose "blind devotion" leads to "awkward exchanges" — warm, wry, lightly quirky rather than heavy or stylized.

on-behalf-of-my-son.rationale: A 178-minute Brazilian "meditation on guilt, grief" told "with remarkable feeling and restraint," following a mother seeking forgiveness from victims' families.

double-freedom.rationale: Alonso's Wavelengths echo of La libertad, a slow 35mm day-in-the-life with non-professional actors, "invigorating rejection of traditional narrative" and a quietly moving meditation on care and freedom.

ancestors.rationale: "Mesmerizing journey through a dreamlike 1980s London" where "memory and longing become impossible to separate" — a slow, visionary AIDS-legacy elegy, "heartbreaking without ever surrendering to despair."

marie-madeleine.rationale: Haitian-Creole reimagining of Mary Magdalene with "moments of sublime surrealism," saturated colour and a city-as-character soundscape; sensual, festive but weighted by religious repression and violence.

the-idiots.rationale: Period literary biopic of Dostoevsky's gambling addiction and his wife Anna, "consumed by art but entangled in a chaotic relationship" — conventional prestige drama at 148 min, largely in English.

the-surgeon.rationale: A "pulse-pounding" "scalp 'em up" with Michelle Yeoh, breathless fight scenes, extreme violence and needle drops — pure genre blockbuster with conventional form.

villeneuve-the-rise-of-a-legend.rationale: "Adrenaline-charged biopic" of Gilles Villeneuve, conventional rise-and-tragic-end sports narrative in French with racing spectacle.

arne-goes-to-space.rationale: "Delightfully odd yet warm-hearted" deadpan Swedish small-town surrealism about elderly brothers and a crash-landed alien, slow-paced with illness undertones.

toy-gun-bandit.rationale: "Wildly energetic" Quebec crime comedy with "escalating mayhem" and "restless, reckless vitality," balanced by warmth and a drug-addiction downward trajectory.

evil-genius.rationale: True-crime dramatization "reminiscent of the Coen Brothers at their most cunningly funny," "brimming with bloodshed, betrayals," with a Gala star cast and non-linear backtracking structure.

phoolan.rationale: An "immersive, taut thriller" built on a 48-hour siege, with Mehta's "restrained and realistic true-crime sensibilities" and heavy caste/sexual-violence trauma, in Hindi at 143 minutes.

your-mother-your-mother-your-mother.rationale: An "audaciously inventive Texas-set action thriller" and "wild ride, overflowing with spectacle and suspense, tenderness and violence" with Mahershala Ali as a gun-averse hitman.

viva-carmen.rationale: Hand-painted French animated Carmen "rendered with expressive brushstrokes" and reframed through children, where "the weight of the original material is still deeply felt" against its violence.

the-road-not-taken.rationale: "Polished and emotionally charged family drama" about early-onset Alzheimer's, 165 min in Chinese, intimate character drama with commercial appeal and only faint formal disorientation.

the-remotes.rationale: "Spacious and elliptical" 183-min Wavelengths hybrid of sci-fi/noir procedural, hypnotic night drives and "post-colonial grief" in Tagalog.

2-6-seconds-death-in-the-outback.rationale: "Gripping" true-crime-adjacent docuseries (two episodes, 148 min) reconstructing a police shooting with body-cam footage — "confronting" collective grief, some Warlpiri language.

the-liberation.rationale: A "devastating look" at cult manipulation and grief, 154 minutes of performance-driven drama with unsettling, thriller-adjacent menace but conventional form.

idda.rationale: "Languidly mysterious portrait" of a simmering female friendship climbing Etna, understated violence and a devastating loss, in Italian with a meandering, portentous camera.

growth-of-the-soil.rationale: A 185-minute "fervently realistic" period epic of homesteading hardship in northern Norway, played with "grace and gravity" in conventional narrative form.

misty-green.rationale: A "hilarious, scathing satire" of Hollywood bigotry with hustle-driven momentum, but weighted by eviction, bipolar crisis, and a "heinous" offer.

lemonade.rationale: Tender social-realist debut about an Irish care leaver that finds "warmth, humour, romance, and gentle beauty in everyday moments" rather than grimness, observational at 142 minutes with Barry Keoghan grounding it.

nosotros.rationale: A quiet, restrained Guatemalan debut of "nuance, restraint, and clarity" about migration, loneliness, and a fragile trans romance amid homophobic hostility.

closing-night.rationale: A "wickedly entertaining family drama" of "deliciously barbed exchange[s]" that turns compassionate — conventional dialogue-driven ensemble piece, 145 min, English-language.

future-tense.rationale: A "thrilling journey through time" sci-fi from Jenna Cato Bass, mixing climate-collapse dread and colonial violence with romance, partly in Xhosa and Afrikaans.

zjili-a-story-of-sisterhood-and-the-burd.rationale: Social-realist Ghanaian drama of kayayei porters told "without sensationalism or artifice," 149 min in Dagbani/Twi, grounded in research and dedicated to a woman who died under a load.

short-cuts-2026-programme-05.rationale: Note is boilerplate mission text with no film detail; placements default to Short Cuts shorts-programme averages of mixed tone and moderate formal play.

a-talent-for-murder.rationale: "Smouldering chamber thriller" of two-hander verbal duelling with "brilliant twists and trenchant dialogue," wickedly witty rather than kinetic, English-language, adapted from a stage play.

tenzing.rationale: Sweeping 158-minute conventional biopic of Tenzing Norgay, "gorgeously photographed" and "inspiring," with survival-adventure stakes but no formal risk.

trees-are-watching.rationale: "Cannily blending psychological horror with local myth" in "surreal set pieces" of "heightened phantasmagoric stylization" and Grand Guignol, from a major Kurdish-Iranian auteur, largely in Kurdish/Turkish.

wavelengths-2-this-suffocating-now.rationale: Wavelengths shorts programme of essay films and in-camera experiments — Tafakory's "layered, lucid essay film," Kosugi's 8mm lyricism, night-vision strolls, and a "visceral" political accusation.

masc.rationale: "Striking, deeply original debut" structured in five chapters shot over a year, an observational portrait "not around crisis or coming out" but subtler identity work, with an "unexpected finale" beyond words.

faith.rationale: British social realism of "unimaginable weight of grief" told with "remarkable rigour" and "grounded realism," heartbreaking and elusive rather than propulsive.

neil-peart-no-ones-disciple.rationale: Conventional music doc with "exhilarating performance sequences" and a "more joyful than mournful" vibe, though it covers Peart's grief and death.

purgatory.rationale: A "charming, gentle, and funny" 1980s coming-of-age dramedy in the Lady Bird/Eighth Grade mode, conventional in form with a 134-min runtime.

a-girl-unknown.rationale: A "quiet, painful, yet ultimately hopeful coming-of-age story" in chapters across 158 minutes, tracing abandonment and displacement with restrained performances in Chinese.

union-town.rationale: "Invigorating" vérité labour doc by two-time Oscar winner Barbara Kopple, winding three NYC union campaigns together over years; observational, conventional form, some Spanish, 136 min.

the-world-before.rationale: Quiet Korean island coming-of-age where "the camera often remains still and attentive" and drama is found in the everyday, tender and bittersweet across 145 minutes.

prima-facie.rationale: A "piercing legal drama" about a barrister who becomes the accuser, "devastating" and "hard-hitting" in a conventional star-vehicle courtroom register.

atonement.rationale: Star-driven Gala drama of war guilt and reconciliation, "searing real-life story" of trauma at 148 min, conventional in form with some Arabic dialogue.

magazine.rationale: A talky, observational debut about a poet intern's "sentimental education" in the pre-#MeToo literary scene — conventional narrative, socially barbed, with a longish 135-minute runtime.

always-lalisa.rationale: Glossy insider pop-star doc with "incredible performances" and behind-the-scenes footage, conventional in form, partly Thai/Korean-language, and pitched as "the ultimate reward" for fans.

head-to-head.rationale: A Persian-language "film within a film" that makes "brilliant use of humour" to satirize male directors' portrayal of women and Iranian censorship, mockery rising alongside real political weight.

la-bola-negra.rationale: A 185-minute "sweeping and operatic" triptych of Lorca-inspired queer repression under fascism, "punctuated by the lasting tragedy of Lorca's execution," with converging storylines and starry cast.

report-to-mother.rationale: A "rich mix of documentary realism and fiction" with "structural rhythms" and cinéma vérité workers'-struggle footage, black-and-white natural-light Malayalam political cinema in 4K restoration.

the-diary-of-a-chambermaid.rationale: Jude's "slapstick skewering of modern-day slavery" in Wavelengths — a formally provocative, talky French/Romanian satire that is also "surprisingly tender."

light-pillar.rationale: "Melancholic, visually audacious meditation on alienation" with hand-drawn animation for reality and live action for VR — formally daring, quietly immersive, slow and wistful.

yaga.rationale: A Baba Yaga-inflected small-town detective story that "blends elements of horror and whodunnit," with wry banter and a "preternatural air" of lurking monstrosity.

short-cuts-2026-programme-01.rationale: Note is boilerplate mission statement with no content; placements are Short Cuts programme priors — mixed shorts, some formal play and international work.

iron-boy.rationale: Hand-painted animated coming-of-age memoir, "beautiful and whimsical," French-language Cannes Special Jury Prize winner from an ex-Pixar animator.

neverman.rationale: A "cold, austere, and threatening institution" holds a trans elder with worsening Alzheimer's, told in flashbacks — heavy, largely conventional drama with a faint thriller edge.

whatcha-want.rationale: A "light touch" crowd-pleaser about a woman in a "gilded cage" rediscovering dance, with "nods to Crazy Rich Asians and Flashdance" and partial Cantonese/Mandarin dialogue.

happily-ever-after.rationale: Family drama about two sisters with "the perfect balance of humour and emotional tension," described as "engaging and approachable," conventionally told in Mandarin.

sisters.rationale: Spanish/Basque family drama of sexual assault and trial with "observational approach" and "measured sadness" — heavy, deliberate, subtitled, conventionally told.

wavelengths-1-house-and-home.rationale: Wavelengths shorts programme of "poetic, tactile" essay films on shelter and memory, mixing archival rumination with "resolutely incensed" political chronicle.

the-final-act.rationale: A contemplative doc on medically assisted death that "creates a space for contemplation," heavy but "suffused with warmth," from a two-time Best Canadian Feature winner.

woman-unknown.rationale: A "gripping," "ever-escalating" postwar Copenhagen thriller of dread and mob retribution, conventionally told in Danish at 156 minutes with "harrowing sequences."

below.rationale: Newfoundland family drama fused with "the chilly depths of marine monstrousness" — conventional creature-feature storytelling balancing warmth and dread.

bas-book.rationale: A "documentary recreation inside a documentary" of a father's memoir, warm and reflective rather than propulsive, largely in Vietnamese with family reenactment scaffolding its formal play.
